terms.comment: A town takes no preposition: Chicāgum (to), Chicāgī (at), Chicāgō (from). Traupman’s adjective is Chicāgēnsis (p. 211).
Egger spells the name as it sounds.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Illinois: Chicago.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
